questions.subject: Hashing
questions.question: Explain the difference between separate chaining and linear probing in Hashing.
questions.ideal_answer: separate chaining and linear probing differ in several ways: separate chaining is linked list collision handling (works by each bucket is a list) whereas linear probing is sequential slot checking (works by simple but causes primary clustering). separate chaining is typically used for O(1 + alpha) average search, while linear probing is used for h(k, i) = (h(k) + i) % m. Example demonstrating separate chaining: List<Node>[] table; // array of linked lists. Example demonstrating linear probing: int idx = (hash + i) % capacity;.

questions.question: Explain the difference between open addressing and double hashing in Hashing.
questions.ideal_answer: open addressing and double hashing differ in several ways: open addressing is probe sequence collision handling (works by finding next empty slot) whereas double hashing is two hash function probing (works by reducing clustering). open addressing is typically used for linear, quadratic, double hashing probes, while double hashing is used for h(k, i) = (h1(k) + i*h2(k)) % m. Example demonstrating open addressing: int probe(int h, int i) { return (h + i) % m; }. Example demonstrating double hashing: int idx = (hash1 + i * hash2) % capacity;.

questions.subject: Hashing
questions.question: Explain the difference between consistent hashing and rolling hash in Hashing.
questions.ideal_answer: consistent hashing and rolling hash differ in several ways: consistent hashing is distributed hash table (works by minimal reorganization on node change) whereas rolling hash is sliding window hash computation (works by O(1) hash update). consistent hashing is typically used for hash ring, virtual nodes, while rolling hash is used for remove leftmost contribution, add rightmost. Example demonstrating consistent hashing: md5(key) mapped to ring; find clockwise node. Example demonstrating rolling hash: hash = (hash - leftChar * pow^(m-1)) * base + rightChar.
